video.title: Inside the $2 Billion Side Hustle Paying People to Eat Out & Drive Around

summary: The episode explains how mystery shopping works, from finding legitimate providers and completing assignments to combining nearby jobs into routes. Guest Mercedes describes common assignments such as apartment tours, car washes, website evaluations and travel, and shares earnings examples from her own work and shoppers in her network. She also describes iShop, her training and recruiting business, and ShopQuest, a free job-listing aggregator for shoppers. The central takeaway is to start with a few legitimate providers, do reliable work, and build a reputation; the income examples are claims, not guaranteed results.

ideas.delivery: The shopper visits or evaluates a business, often without revealing the assignment, records details such as staff names or photos when requested, then completes the provider's report. Assignments described include apartments, car washes, restaurants, gas stations, movie theaters, auto businesses, resorts, and website walkthroughs. Some can be done online; many require travel and in-person work.

Guest reports a personal best of $600 in one day from a car-wash route.
Guest reports earning $300 for a 30-minute website evaluation.
A shopper reportedly earned $850 in less than two days from apartment shops.
A shopper reportedly earned over six figures in a year; another reportedly earned 65,000 and some change in 2025.

ideas.startup_cost: Not stated. Some assignments require paying for a purchase upfront before reimbursement.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: The guest says shoppers can start taking assignments the same day they contract with a provider; payment timing varies by provider.

acquisition.how: Providers post jobs online, but a shopper must choose assignments, apply, and build relationships and reputation.

onboarding.how: Some training and applications can be online, but the shopper must understand each provider's instructions and eligibility rules.

delivery.how: Most work requires a person to visit a location, act as a customer, observe staff, and capture requested evidence. Online evaluations still require human judgement.

billing.how: Providers handle payment, but schedules and methods vary; shoppers may need to track purchases and reimbursements.

support.how: A shopper must resolve assignment questions, correct report issues, and communicate with providers or a training organization.

uk_applicability.notes: The model can operate in the UK, and the guest mentions a shopper visiting the UK. The discussed provider network and many examples are US-focused, so a UK founder would need local provider access, job coverage, and UK-specific handling of expenses and tax.

risks: Income and assignment availability are irregular and depend on location, provider, and the shopper's ability to qualify for jobs.
Travel, mileage, time spent writing reports, and purchases awaiting reimbursement can reduce the effective return.
A report that misses instructions or has poor chronology or grammar may be returned or rejected, and the guest says incorrect work may go unpaid.
Some shops require upfront purchases, so shoppers must be sure they are working with a legitimate provider and understand reimbursement terms.
In-person work and repeated visits can expose a shopper's identity; providers use rotation and may bar a shopper from repeating a location for a period.

tactics.name: Start with a small set of providers
steps: Find a mystery shopping organization or provider with legitimate partnerships.
Register directly on a handful of provider websites.
Complete a few assignments to learn the process before expanding to more providers.

quote.text: I would suggest starting off with a few and then going from there 'cause what happens, you can get overwhelmed.
quote.speaker: Mercedes

tactics.name: Build routes from separate assignments
steps: Choose a day for assignments.
Combine nearby shops from multiple providers into one route.
Mix assignment types when practical, such as an apartment visit, meal shop, and gas station shop.
Account for travel and report-writing time when deciding whether a route is worthwhile.

quote.text: you can piece together different types of shops. So a lot of times like when I would go out, I would do apartment mystery shops.
quote.speaker: Mercedes

tactics.name: Protect shopper reputation
steps: Accept assignments only when you can complete them.
Follow the assignment instructions, document the requested details, and submit reports on time.
Write clear, chronological narratives when the report asks for them.
Meet provider representatives through industry organizations and conferences.

quote.text: The key is to number one, do good work, right? Don't flake out on shops that you have to do.
quote.speaker: Mercedes

tactics.name: Screen out mystery shopping scams
steps: Treat a check sent before work as a warning sign, especially if you are told to cash it and send money elsewhere.
Do not buy gift cards and send the redemption codes.
Check whether the sender's email domain matches the real company domain.
Use an organization that can confirm its provider partnerships.

quote.text: Common Sense tells us jobs and companies don't typically pay you before you go and do your work.
quote.speaker: Mercedes

tactics.name: Track mileage and expenses
steps: Use a mileage-tracking tool to record business travel.
Track required purchases and reimbursement status.
Check each provider's pay schedule and payment method before accepting assignments.

quote.text: There's a lot. I mean, you've got mile IQ that shoppers love to use
quote.speaker: Mercedes

tactics.name: Use training to reduce avoidable report errors
steps: Teach shoppers how to complete an assignment from start to finish.
Practice writing complete, chronological narratives.
Explain provider instructions and report requirements before shoppers accept work.

tactics.name: Build a directory around the provider fragmentation
steps: Identify that shoppers must register with many providers and search each website.
Aggregate available jobs by shopper location.
Add useful filters and features based on shopper requests.
Keep listing data current as providers add and remove assignments.

Third-party mystery shopping apps may not show all available jobs and may surface lower-paying assignments.

Some providers rotate shoppers or restrict repeat visits to keep employees from recognizing the shopper.
The guest sells paid training and promotes ShopQuest, so her recommendations and success stories have a promotional interest.

evidence_quality.rationale: The guest describes over a decade of personal mystery shopping, gives concrete assignment workflows, and explains how her training and recruiting business operates. Several earnings and demand figures are reported from shoppers, company data, or a company vice president and are not independently verified; one earnings range appears misheard in the transcript.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Mercedes sells paid training through iShop and promotes the free ShopQuest directory. The host also reads paid sponsor endorsements for Gusto, Wealthfront, Quo, and Shopify.
